unsupported.reason: A single electricity price change does not identify the provincial market, regulated tariff, fuel cost or generation constraint. No common national electricity-to-GDP coefficient is estimated.

methodology.outcome: 100 × log(real GDP at market prices in t+h / real GDP in t−1), million chained 2017 CAD levels
methodology.features: Intercept, previous annual real GDP log growth and annual nominal US-dollar energy-price log change
methodology.interpretation: Conditional historical association. The response compares the fitted GDP level under a price change with the same fitted model under an unchanged price. It is not a causal impact or an adjustment to the independent provincial forecast.
methodology.pricePath: The regressor changes the price-change year annual average. Later energy prices are unconditioned. Horizons do not represent a persistent or temporary price-path intervention.
variants: Equal blend of own and peer-group pooled slopes
Peer-group pooled slopes with province intercepts
methodology.groupRule: Fixed research groups for principal oil-producing provinces and Western Canadian gas-producing provinces. No group is chosen from GDP fit scores. Territories use own-region models.
methodology.selection: At each historical origin, choose the price-model variant with lowest mean absolute error over earlier origins whose GDP outcome year has ended. Use own-province OLS until five such evaluations exist. Choose the no-price AR variant separately by the same rule. Final fit uses all completed evaluations.
methodology.training: Training outcomes end strictly before the held-out price-change year. Minimum own-province rows are 18 for oil and 12 for gas. Evaluation begins no earlier than 2006.
methodology.validationScope: The held-out year energy price is treated as already observed. These are conditional historical tests using latest-vintage GDP, not forecasts available at the start of that year or vintage-real-time tests.
methodology.screenInterpretation: An application evidence screen, not proof of causality or future accuracy. It compares with both a historical mean and a separately selected no-price autoregression; all attempts remain published.
methodology.rangeInterpretation: Parameter ranges hold the selected model fixed. Separate outcome-error ranges come from previous conditional prediction errors. They must not be exchanged or called causal confidence bounds.
limitations: Supply and demand causes of energy prices are not identified. Global activity, exchange rates, weather, fiscal changes and other common influences can explain associations.

The annual data sample is small. The grouping and candidate family were researched using this history; nested selection prevents future outcomes entering an origin but cannot erase research design reuse.
Revised historical GDP and current data vintages are used. No historical release-vintage database is reconstructed.
The 80% bootstrap range excludes model-selection uncertainty. The empirically targeted 80% outcome range does not guarantee 80% future coverage.
Nominal US-dollar benchmark changes are associated with real Canadian-dollar GDP. They do not estimate the effect of an isolated exchange-rate-adjusted domestic price intervention.
The following-year outcome accumulates GDP changes across two years. It does not assume the initial price change persists.
